_comment: Matrise policy - example for an AD-managed estate.
Copy to policy.json next to the app, or publish it on a read-only share and
point the MATRISE_POLICY environment variable at it (deploy that variable
with the app through Software Center / Intune).
This file governs what the CONSOLE offers. It is not a security boundary on
its own - anyone who can run PowerShell can ignore it. Generate the JEA
endpoint from this same file so the endpoint enforces the same list:
Rule matching, most specific first: id > pattern > group/section > impact.

rules.reason: Rebuilds the network stack and needs a reboot. Run remotely, it drops the very connection you are working over and leaves the machine unreachable until someone walks to it. Deskside only.
Moving a suspected binary destroys the evidence DFIR needs and tips off anything watching. Isolate the machine and hand it to the IR team instead.
Schedules an offline disk check. The machine is unusable for hours on next boot, so the user needs warning first.
Changes the security posture of a managed endpoint. Those settings come from GPO here, so this either fights policy or hides a GPO that is not applying.
Overwrites the HOSTS file. Some line-of-business apps still depend on entries there.
Long-running or reboot-required. Fine to run, but the user should be told before it starts.
